name: Lorencia
note: The world's manifest (docs/order-plan.md, sprint D). `show` is MapShow, read by game/world/world_show.cpp: what the client draws, plays and hears here. A system opens only where its field is set. Copied to assets/world/<w>/world.json by tools/sync.sh.

rules.note: mu.db's gates table, the spawn rows: 17  map 0  133,118 to 151,135   Lorencia 27  map 3  171,108 to 177,117   Noria 22  map 2  197,35 to 218,50     Devias Lorencia's 142,126 is the tile the world has always opened on, and it is inside gate 17; kept so a character made before this table comes in where he always did. Devias is last so the M key still goes Lorencia to Noria first. The Golden Dragon invades here, on its own clock (sim/invasion.h; OpenMU VersionSeasonSix InvasionMobsInitialization.cs:74-101): Lorencia first, Devias and Noria since 2026-10-08 (the user: 'dragon can land on devias,lorencia,noria').

npcs.name: Orsin the Broker
npcs.note: Ours: the Broker (sim::kBroker, docs/broker.md), the market Lorencia, Devias and Noria share, three tiles east of Baz so the vault and the market stand together (the user, 2026-10-11). Moved to 140,139, on the street by the fenced garden (the user, 2026-10-12: 'move broker here in lorencia'). Look 4 to 3, facing up the street toward one who comes to him from the garden's corner ('rotate broker so he is facing character'). Not a MU NPC; he wears MuMain's Mirage (Npc/mirazu.bmd, scale 0.95), the user's pick, the same figure in all three towns.

exits.note: Gates.cs, CreateTargetGates. Lorencia's 26 is Direction.West (1), which points at (-1,-1), up the map and away from gate 23 below it; Noria's 24 is Direction.East (5), (+1,+1), down the map and away from gate 25 above it. Either way he comes out facing into the map. Lorencia, from Noria

Lorencia's west edge and Devias's east edge. 21 is Direction.South (3), (+1,-1), into Lorencia and away from gate 18 beside it; 19 is Direction.North (7), (-1,+1), into Devias and away from gate 20. Lorencia, from Devias
The Dungeon's, Gates.cs:114 and 119-125. 1 West is (-1,-1) and 3 South (+1,-1), each facing away from the enter box beside it. Lorencia's 4 is in front of DoungeonGate01. Lorencia, out of the Dungeon

enters.note: Gates.cs, CreateEnterGates: 23 on Lorencia's last rows, 25 on Noria's first, each two rows past its exit gate so a character who comes out is not sent straight back, and each asks level 10. Every level here is MU's doubled, ours (the user, 2026-10-04: 'also increase other gate requirments because we have fast paced exp gains', after Atlans's 60 went to 120): the experience rate is 100x (sim kExperienceRate). The free ways out stay free. Atlans's way in is 70 and its way back keeps 60, below. Lorencia to Noria
Gates.cs:193-194. Lorencia's asks level 15; the way back asks nothing. Lorencia to Devias

Gates.cs:185, Lorencia's stair down at DoungeonGate01, level 20, to the Dungeon's exit gate 2. And the Dungeon's own, :186-192: the way out asks nothing, every stair between its three floors asks level 20. Floors are regions of one map, so 5 to 15 lead to the map they stand on (Realm::throughGate). Lorencia to Dungeon 1

spawn.note: OpenMU's spawn gate 17: the box a new character starts in and a dead one stands up in, the .mur's safe gate (pipeline/index.py gate_rows). rules.arrive is its middle. Out of mu.db's gates table in sprint D6.

hidden.note: Placement types that exist in the map and are never drawn (terrain.py's old HIDDEN_TYPES): PoseBox01 at 133, invisible walls that give a sitting or leaning player something to sit down on -- 53 of them; Light01 to Light03 at 130 to 132 are anchors for fire: MoveObject calls CreateFire on each and hides the model in the same breath. Carried through with a flag rather than dropped: the 25 fire anchors are the map telling us where its braziers are.

perches.note: Lorencia: 53 hidden pose boxes along the walls, the river's logs, the tavern benches Here for one reason only (terrain.py's old OPERABLE_TYPES): their tiles must never be stamped NoMove. The client gates the click on the placement's own tile and walks the character onto it; MU's grid leaves those tiles open on purpose, and the solid-stamping pass would close 24 of the 110 behind its back (index.py stamp_blocked).
